_meta.indication: REDEMPLO is indicated as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial; patients received four total doses of REDEMPLO 25 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously once every 3 months over a 12-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with genetically confirmed or clinically diagnosed familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) with screening fasting TG >= 880 mg/dL refractory to lipid-lowering therapy, maintained on a low-fat diet; mean baseline fasting TG 2,311 mg/dL.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was percent change in fasting triglycerides from baseline at Month 10 (average of 2 assessments, 2 to 7 days apart).
pivotal_trials.n: N=51 randomized to the approved regimen analysis (REDEMPLO 25 mg n=26, placebo n=25)
pivotal_trials.result: Median difference between REDEMPLO 25 mg and placebo in percent change in fasting triglycerides from baseline to Month 10 was -58.7% (95% CI: -89.6, -27.9; p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and >5% more than placebo) were hyperglycemia (20% vs 8% placebo), headache (16% vs 8%), nausea (14% vs 8%), and injection site reaction (10% vs 4%). Adverse reactions led to discontinuation in 3 (6.0%) REDEMPLO-treated patients (hyperglycemia and urticaria) vs 0% placebo.
target_moa: Plozasiran is an apoC-III-directed siRNA conjugated with GalNAc that degrades apoC-III mRNA through RNA interference, reducing hepatic and serum apoC-III protein, which leads to increased clearance of serum triglycerides.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety data did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class and there were no controversial issues.

summary.text: Plozasiran (REDEMPLO) was granted Orphan Drug Designation (June 2019), Fast Track designation (March 2023), and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (September 2024) for FCS; NDA 219947 was received November 18, 2024, filed with no filing review issues, and approved via traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on one adequate and well-controlled trial (AROAPOC3-3001) plus confirmatory evidence.

citations.quote: On June 20, 2019, Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals received Orphan Drug Designation for plozasiran for the treatment of FCS.

On February 2, 2023, Arrowhead submitted a request for Fast Track designation for the treatment of FCS. This request was granted on March 17, 2023, for reducing triglycerides in adult patients with FCS.

On July 18, 2024, Arrowhead submitted a request for Breakthrough Therapy Designation for FCS. This request was granted on September 9, 2024, for ARO-APOC3 as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with FCS.
